solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Out of debt, having a little money in store, initially

indicators.note: the word a is placed first, ahead of the money

parts.note: a float is the small stock of cash kept in a shop till for change

explanation.surface: Someone solvent again, with a small cash reserve put away at the start.
explanation.definitionFit: To stay afloat financially is an idiom for remaining solvent rather than sinking into debt.

clue.text: A message about temperature I had, providing remedy

indicators.note: the message goes around, so it surrounds the temperature and I had

parts.note: a note is a short written message
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: A doctor's note mentioning a fever, suggesting a cure.
explanation.definitionFit: An antidote is a substance that counteracts a poison, so a cure or remedy.

clue.text: Lights falling on part of costume and painted scenery

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: to light on something is to land on it, so lights means lands
a cape is a cloak worn as part of a costume

explanation.surface: Stage lighting shining on an actor's costume and the painted backdrop.
explanation.definitionFit: A landscape is a picture of rural scenery, as painted by an artist.

clue.text: Man housing very systematic record collection

indicators.note: the man's name contains the next piece as a house holds its occupant

parts.note: Archie is a man's name

explanation.surface: A man keeping a very orderly collection of vinyl records.
explanation.definitionFit: An archive is an organised store of historical documents and records.

clue.text: Conservative politician guarded by distant PC, perhaps

indicators.note: the politician is enclosed by the word for distant, as if surrounded by guards

parts.note: outer means further out, distant
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A Tory politician being protected by a remote police constable.
explanation.walkthrough: PC looks like police constable in the surface; here it is a personal computer.
explanation.definitionFit: A PC, personal computer, is one example of a computer, hence the 'perhaps'.

clue.text: Exploded courts into bits, delaying legal process

indicators.note: something exploded is blown apart, so these letters are scattered and reassembled

explanation.surface: A bomb blowing courtrooms to pieces, holding up the justice system.
explanation.definitionFit: An obstructionist deliberately blocks or stalls proceedings, such as legislation, by delaying tactics.

clue.text: He, for example, is supporting no multinational organisation

parts.note: pro means in favour of, supporting
UN is the United Nations

explanation.surface: A man who backs no international body.
explanation.definitionFit: 'He' is a personal pronoun, a word standing in for a noun, so it is one example.

clue.text: Number coming from North and South — meeting in the middle, in principle

indicators.text: coming from North and South — meeting in the middle
indicators.note: the number is read down from the top and also up from the bottom of this down entry, the two readings sharing their central letter

parts.note: ten is a number; read from either end of the entry it overlaps itself at the middle letter

explanation.surface: A figure approached from both directions converging centrally, in theory.
explanation.walkthrough: TEN read down from the top and TEN read up from the bottom (NET) overlap on the middle N, so the entry reads the same both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenet is a belief or doctrine held as true, a principle.

clue.text: Put in new order for leisure centre

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a holiday ..., a place people go for leisure

explanation.walkthrough: Read as a verb it is sort again, with a hyphen implied; as a noun it is a holiday destination.
explanation.definitionFit: A resort is a holiday destination, while re-sort means arrange once more.

clue.text: Second time I'm into greedy behaviour, being highly mistaken

indicators.note: the first three pieces go inside the word for greedy behaviour

parts.note: overeating is eating too much, gluttony
taken as written, without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A dieter admitting that on a second occasion they are gorging, badly wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Overestimating means judging something too high, so being badly wrong in an inflated direction.

clue.text: Part of uniform cut in a different way

indicators.note: cut in a different way means the letters are reassembled in a new order

explanation.surface: A piece of uniform tailored with a different cut.
explanation.definitionFit: A tunic is a close-fitting jacket worn by soldiers or police as uniform.

clue.text: Noble types opposed to screening one's tally

indicators.note: to screen is to shield or hide behind, so the outer piece wraps the rest

parts.note: vs, versus, means against
one is I, and 's is S
a count is a tally

explanation.surface: Aristocrats objecting to someone hiding their score.
explanation.definitionFit: Viscounts are members of the peerage ranking between earls and barons.

clue.text: Collected documents from vagrant I put inside

indicators.note: the I is placed inside the word for vagrant

parts.note: a dosser is British slang for a homeless person who sleeps rough

explanation.surface: Someone takes papers off a tramp after planting them on him.
explanation.definitionFit: A dossier is a file of papers containing information about a person or subject.

clue.text: List including duck or another domestic fowl

indicators.note: the list contains the duck

parts.note: a roster is a list of duties or names
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so O

explanation.surface: A register of poultry featuring a duck or some other farmyard bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Duck' looks like one of the birds, but it is the cricket term for zero, giving O. 'Another' just distinguishes this bird from the duck.
explanation.definitionFit: A rooster is a cockerel, a male farmyard chicken.

clue.text: Ill-feeling people still do not suffer from

definitions.text: Ill-feeling people still do not suffer from

parts.words: Ill-feeling people still do not suffer from
parts.note: people who stay still, not moving about in vehicles, cannot get nauseous from motion; 'ill-feeling' suggests resentment

explanation.walkthrough: Ill-feeling reads as animosity that people continue to avoid, but it is literal sickness, and 'still' means motionless.
explanation.definitionFit: Travel sickness is nausea caused by the motion of a car, boat or plane, which a stationary person escapes.

clue.text: Edges up to sweetheart, as an unexpected consequence

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: lips are edges, as of a cup or crater
a lover is a sweetheart

explanation.surface: Someone sidling over towards their beloved, with surprising results.
explanation.definitionFit: A spillover is a side effect that spreads beyond its original area, often unforeseen.

clue.text: Against the rules, taking article from France? Quite

parts.note: un is the French indefinite article
fairly means quite, to a moderate degree

explanation.surface: Someone cheating by lifting an item from France, quite so.
explanation.definitionFit: To act unfairly is to act unjustly, breaking the rules of fair play.

clue.text: Improving appearance, you said, added to achievement of venerable status

indicators.note: the letter is put into the longer word

parts.note: beatification is the Catholic step of declaring someone blessed, short of sainthood
U is pronounced like 'you'

explanation.surface: Someone saying their good looks have been boosted by being made nearly a saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Beautification means making something more attractive, improving how it looks.

clue.text: Mythical beast presenting no dilemma?

parts.note: a dilemma has two horns; this creature has only one, so it cannot leave you on the horns of a dilemma

explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on the horns of a dilemma' means facing two bad choices; a one-horned beast offers no such pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a legendary horse-like creature with a single horn on its forehead.

clue.text: Democrat, in one part of chapter, is hostile

indicators.note: the Democrat goes inside the following pieces

parts.note: a means one
a verse is a numbered section of a Bible chapter

explanation.surface: A Democrat featured in a section of some report is antagonistic.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means unfavourable or opposing, as in adverse conditions.

clue.text: Wrongly convicted and prepared for hanging

definitions.meaning: first meaning: falsely set up to be found guilty
second meaning: a picture is ... before going on the wall

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests an innocent being sent to the gallows; the hanging is of a picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A framed person has been incriminated with false evidence, and a framed picture is mounted ready to hang.

clue.text: Model I wrapped in oddly shaped parcel

indicators.note: the I is enclosed by the rearranged letters as by wrapping paper
an odd shape means the letters of the word are reformed

explanation.surface: A model kit packed inside a strangely shaped package.
explanation.definitionFit: A replica is an exact copy or scale model of something.

clue.text: Endangered animal also taken on board by the old man

indicators.note: taken on board means held inside, so the father contains the word for also

parts.note: the old man is informal for father, pa
and means also, in addition

explanation.surface: A rare creature also carried onto a ship by Dad.
explanation.definitionFit: The giant panda is a famous threatened species, the emblem of conservation charities.

clue.text: After first half of month, everyone's back for work in library

parts.note: the first four letters of the eight-letter November

indicators.note: turned back, so the word for everyone is read in reverse

parts.note: all means everyone

explanation.surface: Mid-month, all the staff return to their jobs in the library.
explanation.definitionFit: A novella is a short novel, a piece of fiction you might borrow.

clue.text: Leader of musicians on island adjusted old instruments

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter
adjusted means altered, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: The head of a band on an island retuning some vintage instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandolins are lute-family stringed instruments of long standing, played with a plectrum.

clue.text: King leading state, such as George III

indicators.note: the king's letter goes in front of the word for state

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for Rex, king
aver means to state, assert

explanation.surface: A monarch heading a nation, George III being an example.
explanation.walkthrough: George III is remembered for his bouts of madness; a raver here is a madman, one who raves.
explanation.definitionFit: A raver in the older sense is someone who raves wildly, a lunatic, which George III was reputed to be.

clue.text: System for removing water one installed in a garden, originally

indicators.note: the one is fitted inside the rearranged letters of the garden phrase
done in an original, inventive way, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A garden fitted with a water-removal scheme in the first place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Originally' (done in an original way) rearranges A GARDEN to DRANAGE, and 'installed in' puts I, one, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Drainage is the arrangement of pipes and channels that carries away surplus water.

clue.text: Almost new, and ahead of time

parts.note: early means before the expected time

explanation.surface: Something practically new, and arriving early too.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly means not quite, very close to completely.
